title: Windsurf / Devin Desktop
summary: Windsurf, now named Devin Desktop, retains a full IDE and adds an agent command center.

facts.label: Workflow
facts.value: The official FAQ identifies Devin Desktop as the new name for Windsurf and says the standard update preserves existing plan and pricing, including legacy Windsurf Enterprise. The separate Devin Local agent documentation says Cascade Memories and Workflows are not supported by Devin Local and recommends the Cascade Migration Wizard to migrate them into Skills. This is an agent-selection detail distinct from the standard app update; no account or workflow migration was tested.

facts.label: Privacy / data handling
facts.value: Cognition's Privacy Policy (last updated 2026-03-09) says User Content may be used to train, fine-tune and improve its models depending on the terms that apply. Its Platform Terms (last updated 2026-06-30) define Customer Data to include inputs and outputs and permit model training; paid Service Tiers may opt out, with a Teams administrator required to do so, after which Cognition says provider Zero Data Retention is enabled. The Terms retain exceptions for safety/abuse review and legal process. Cognition's DPA (last updated 2026-07-23) applies to Customer Data processed on a customer's behalf under applicable agreements, limits processing to documented service purposes and requires equivalent subprocessor restrictions preventing Customer Data model training. A separate Windsurf MSA is expressly labeled for Exafunction Services only and says its Customer Data is not used to train models and is deleted after generating output, except for listed persistent features, suspected AUP violations and profile data. These sources describe different data definitions, roles and agreement scopes; no account tier, assignment notice, order form, opt-out setting or enabled persistent feature was checked.

facts.label: Product self-hosting
facts.value: Codeium's current Windsurf Marketplace listing describes its Codeium Enterprise Updater as for self-hosted enterprise customers only. This is bounded evidence of a self-hosted Enterprise customer path for the listed Codeium product. The public listing does not specify deployment architecture, which service components or data are self-hosted, model inference location, whether this path remains available to users of the Devin Desktop continuation, or eligibility for new customers. The older Windsurf plugin setup page redirects and was not used as current evidence. No account or installation was inspected.

sections.heading: Product name and transition
paragraphs: The current official FAQ calls Devin Desktop the new name for Windsurf and says the standard over-the-air update preserves the IDE, extensions, workflows, settings, in-progress work, plans and pricing, including legacy Windsurf Enterprise. This record has not tested an individual account transition.

The separate Devin Local agent runs on the user's machine. Its documentation lists Cascade Memories and Workflows as unsupported by Devin Local and recommends migrating them into Skills; this does not establish where model inference runs.

sections.heading: Keep price and account scope separate
paragraphs: The official plan page lists Free at USD 0/month, Pro at USD 20/month, Max at USD 200/month and Teams at USD 80/month plus USD 40/month per full developer seat. Paid-plan allowances refresh daily and weekly, extra usage can be purchased at API pricing, and actual cost varies by model and task. These public amounts do not establish a specific legacy account's entitlement, regional checkout total or actual spend.

pros.text: The vendor identifies Devin Desktop as the new name for Windsurf and says the IDE experience remains available.
Devin Desktop describes a full IDE with syntax highlighting, autocomplete and debugging tools.
The current public plan page lists Free at USD 0/month, Pro at USD 20/month, Max at USD 200/month and Teams at USD 80/month plus USD 40/month per full developer seat.

Cognition's current Platform Terms allow paid Service Tiers to opt out of Customer Data model training and say the opt-out enables Zero Data Retention with model providers, subject to listed safety and legal exceptions.

The Codeium Marketplace lists an Enterprise updater specifically for self-hosted enterprise customers, a narrow signal that a self-hosted Enterprise customer path exists for the listed Codeium product.
Devin Local is documented as a local agent harness with access to files, tools and the environment on the user's machine; this describes agent execution, not where model inference runs.

cons.text: The standard transition is documented by the vendor, but no account-specific migration or entitlement was independently tested for this review.
Published base prices do not establish a particular legacy Windsurf account's exact entitlement, checkout total or actual usage cost.

Cognition's Platform Terms, DPA and Exafunction-specific Windsurf MSA describe different training and retention conditions; the agreement and settings that apply to an individual account were not inspected.

The public Codeium Enterprise updater listing does not describe deployment topology, service or data placement, inference location, new-customer eligibility or continuity into Devin Desktop; no account or installation was checked.
The Devin Local documentation lists Cascade Memories and Workflows as unsupported by that agent and recommends migrating them into Skills; no account or workflow migration was tested.

faqs.question: Is Devin Desktop the new name for Windsurf?
faqs.answer: Yes. The official FAQ describes Devin Desktop as the new name for Windsurf and says the full IDE remains accessible.

faqs.question: What does the vendor say carries over during the standard update?
faqs.answer: The FAQ says plans, pricing, extensions, settings and in-progress work carry over with the standard over-the-air update, and that current plan pricing stays the same, including legacy Windsurf Enterprise. Confirm the applicable path for the specific account.

faqs.question: What public monthly prices does Devin list for the Windsurf continuation?
faqs.answer: The current plan page lists Free at USD 0/month, Pro at USD 20/month, Max at USD 200/month and Teams at USD 80/month plus USD 40/month per full developer seat. Paid-plan included usage refreshes daily and weekly; extra usage is available at API pricing. These are public plan amounts, not an account-specific legacy quote or total usage estimate.

faqs.question: How do Cognition's training terms apply to Windsurf and Devin Desktop?
faqs.answer: Cognition's Privacy Policy says User Content may be used for training depending on applicable terms. Its June 2026 Platform Terms permit Customer Data training and let paid tiers opt out; Teams requires an administrator, and opting out enables provider Zero Data Retention subject to safety, abuse and legal exceptions. The July 2026 DPA sets separate processing and subprocessor limits for applicable personal Customer Data. Windsurf's MSA says its no-training and output-deletion rules are specific to Exafunction Services, with listed exceptions. Confirm the account's controlling agreement, plan, setting and enabled persistent features; none was inspected here.

faqs.question: What does the official listing establish about self-hosted Enterprise access?
faqs.answer: The Windsurf Marketplace lists a Codeium Enterprise Updater for self-hosted Enterprise customers. This establishes a limited customer-path signal for the listed Codeium product; the public listing does not explain deployment architecture, data or model location, eligibility for new customers, or whether the option continues for Devin Desktop. No account or installation was checked.

faqs.question: Does Devin Local mean model inference runs on your device?
faqs.answer: The Devin Local documentation says its agent harness operates on your machine and can access local files, tools and the environment. The Cascade documentation separately describes model selection, but the reviewed pages do not establish that model inference runs locally or identify a local endpoint. Treat local agent execution as separate from local model inference; no account, model or endpoint was tested.

faqs.question: What happens to Cascade Workflows and Memories when switching to Devin Local?
faqs.answer: Devin's documentation lists Memories and Workflows as unsupported by Devin Local and recommends the Cascade Migration Wizard to migrate them into Skills. This concerns using the Devin Local agent; the Desktop FAQ's separate standard-update statement does not verify a particular account or workflow migration. No account migration was tested.

verdict: Treat Devin Desktop as the documented continuation of Windsurf; use current public plan prices for general comparison, and verify any legacy account quote and usage terms before acting.
bestFor: Existing Windsurf users assessing the documented transition or current editor workflow
notFor: Buyers treating historical Windsurf prices as a current quote
migration: Record the current account and editor settings, confirm the official update applies, and rehearse the workflow before changing a production setup.
gaps: No account-specific transition or legacy entitlement was tested; public base plan prices do not establish the exact account quote, regional checkout taxes or actual usage cost.

Confirm the account's applicable Cognition or Exafunction agreement, Service Tier, any executed DPA or Order Form, model-training opt-out, and enabled persistent features; public documents describe different data scopes and conditions.
